title: Heaplight staging allocator & thread multiplexor to shrink host CPU-GPU handoff
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We observe persistent 10-30% host-side p99 latency spikes during prefill bursts across multi-tenant machines. Root causes: allocator churn and large memcpy fanout from ephemeral staging arenas, plus threadpool contention when many short-lived prefill tasks race to prepare pinned buffers. Goals: design and implement a lightweight staging allocator (Heaplight) with per-socket arenas, a DMA gatekeeper that deduplicates concurrent copies, and a thread multiplexor to reduce context switching and mutex thrash. The implementation should reduce host CPU utilization, lower prefill p99 by at least 20%, and eliminate memcpy storms that correlate with kernel dispatch jitter.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end prefill p99 reduced by >=20% on benchmark workload (mixed short+long prompts) compared to baseline. 2) Host CPU user/sys utilization during burst reduced by >=25%. 3) No regressions in decode throughput and GPU occupancy. 4) Integration tests covering arena rollover, max resident set, DMA dedupe correctness, and thread multiplexor starvation scenarios. 5) Rollout flags exist to toggle Heaplight per cluster and a telemetry dashboard capturing allocator churn, DMA dedupe hit rate, and threadpool queueing latency.
technical_notes: - Heaplight design: per-NUMA socket slab arenas with power-of-two bucket sizes tuned for common prefill sizes (128B, 512B, 2KB, 16KB, 64KB). Use lock-free freelists for hot paths and a fallback spinlock for cold paths. Arena lifetime aligned to microbatch lifecycle to encourage reuse without unbounded growth. - DMA gatekeeper: maintain short-lived copy-key dedupe map keyed by (src_addr, dst_buf_id, length, sequence_id) to coalesce duplicate memcpys from concurrent prefill tasks. Use epoch-based reclamation to avoid locks in hot path. - Thread multiplexor: single worker per NUMA socket multiplexes many prefill subtasks via cooperative coroutines; worker yields before GPU dispatch. This flattens the threadcount and reduces scheduler churn. - NUMA awareness: allocator and multiplexor bind to socket-local cpus and pin pinned buffers to socket-local devices where possible. - Safety: ensure memory fences for concurrent KV cache updates; expose backpressure to caller when staging pool exhausted (fail-fast with retry suggestion). - Telemetry: allocator hits/misses, peak arena size, DMA dedupe rate, multiplexor queue length, per-socket CPU load.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Spike, 1 week): bench synthetic prefill patterns to tune bucket sizes and measure freelist contention. Phase 2 (Prototype, 2 weeks): implement Heaplight arenas + unit tests; integrate with prefill path behind feature flag. Phase 3 (DMA gatekeeper, 2 weeks): implement dedupe map and end-to-end correctness tests. Phase 4 (Thread multiplexor, 2 weeks): replace short-lived thread spawns with cooperative worker on a feature-flagged path; validate latency/throughput. Phase 5 (Hardening & rollout, 1 week): add telemetry, rollout gating, docs, run canary on dedicated capacity. Each phase includes performance benchmarks and safety tests. Rollout strategy: canary to 5% of traffic -> 25% -> 100% with automated revert on p99 regressions.
test_plan: - Unit tests: freelist correctness, arena rollover, memory accounting, DMA dedupe correctness under simulated concurrency. - Integration tests: multi-tenant prefill bursts, simulate OOM in staging pool and assert fail-fast semantics. - Load tests: run production-like workloads on staging cluster and compare p50/p95/p99 and GPU occupancy. - Chaos tests: random thread preemption, forced NUMA migration, and simulated partial DMA failures to validate graceful fallback to memcpy. - CI gating: require no new flaky tests and baseline perf must not regress on nightly benchmark.
metrics_targets: prefill_p99: -20% or better; host_cpu_util_peak: -25% or better; dma_dedupe_hit_rate: >=40% on synthetic dedupe patterns; staging_pool_oom_rate: 0 (should be handled by backpressure).
